title: fix(plugin-list): a map list view projects its location bindings (objectui#10370)
body:
Fixes #10370
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`ListView`'s `$select` view-binding arm had no `map` entry, and its candidate keys named none of the map's bindings. A map view whose authored columns omit the location field therefore sent `$select: ['id', ...columns]`. On a backend that honours `$select`, every row arrived without coordinates, and `ObjectMap` (which draws from the host rows) placed no marker.

Both collectors in `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` now have a map arm:

- **`$select` arm (`selectFields`):** `collectViewFields(resolveListMapConfig(schema))`. The candidate list gains `locationField`, `latitudeField`, `longitudeField` and `descriptionField`, the keys `ObjectMap` reads off a row (`extractCoordinates` and the marker description). `titleField` was already a candidate. Every name goes through `addSpeculative`: the known-field gate first, then FLS.
- **`expandFields` twin:** the same call. Its candidate list gains the three coordinate keys, and deliberately NOT `descriptionField` (measured below).
- **Both dependency lists** (the `$expand` memo and the fetch effect) gain `schema.map`, the typed key the capability gate's memo already names.

## Why the resolver, not the two blocks one at a time

Triage execution point 1 asks for both blocks, covering "the spellings the map config resolver actually reads". `resolveListMapConfig` is that resolver: the render branch and the capability gate both call it. It reads `schema.options?.map` and `schema.map` through the declared-key whitelist and merges them per key, with the view-level block winning. Calling it collects both blocks, and exactly the bindings the markers are drawn from. The sibling convention (a union of both blocks) would also request a bag value that the view-level block shadows, which nothing reads. A pin checks that the shadowed value is not requested.

| spelling | read by the map | projected now |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `map.locationField`; `map.latitudeField` + `map.longitudeField` | yes (spec `ListMapConfigSchema`) | yes |
| `options.map.*` (the producer bag app-shell's `ObjectView` writes) | yes | yes |
| a split pair across the two | yes (per-key merge) | yes |
| a top-level `locationField` | no: the spec list view refuses it by name (`unrecognized_keys`), and no map branch reads it | no (control pin) |

The card's probe listed "a flat `locationField`" as its first spelling. If that meant a top-level key, it is the last row: that view renders the map's "configuration required" refusal whatever the projection is, so there is nothing to project. Covering it would add a consumer-side alias for a refused key.

## The `$expand` twin, measured

Any of the map keys can name a lookup. I measured each key's effect on the real `ObjectMap` with a one-shot, uncommitted probe that fed it host rows and clicked a marker:

- **Description, expanded lookup `{ id, name }`:** the render throws `Objects are not valid as a React child`.
- **Description, bare id `'a1'`:** the popup renders `Harbour Depota1`.
- **Title:** `getRecordDisplayName` resolves an embedded object to its display name, so expanding a title lookup improves it.
- **Coordinates:** `extractCoordinates` reads a `{ lat, lng }` object. A bare id places nothing either way.

So the twin collects the coordinate keys and the existing `titleField`, but never `descriptionField`. Expanding the description would open a new route to that crash, for a map whose columns omit a lookup-typed description. The `$select` arm still projects it.

## Tests (head `16865773b`)

- **Reproduction at base `d3d134b47`:** the new pin file gave 9 failed | 5 passed (14). Every map spelling gave `$select` `['id', 'subject']`.
- **Package suites:** `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-list/ packages/plugin-map/` from the repo root gave Test Files 115 passed (115) and Tests 1219 passed (1219).
- **Tests that read plugin-list source from disk:** these are the test files matching `readFileSync|readdirSync` and also naming `plugin-list` or `ListView.tsx`, outside those two packages. All 27 files passed.
- **Type-check:** I built the dependency closure first (`turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/plugin-list^...'`, 12/12 tasks). Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-list run type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exited 0. `--listFilesOnly` shows the test project compiles the new pin file.
- **eslint** (`--no-inline-config`, 2 files):
  - Per-rule counts on `ListView.tsx` are identical to base, with 0 errors.
  - The new test carries 3 `no-explicit-any` warnings. They are the same stub casts its sibling `ListView.allDeniedSelect-10275.test.tsx` uses.
  - Evidence that the narrowed run covers everything this diff can affect: eslint's own config resolves the file (`--print-config`); `--format json` counts 2 files; `parserOptions` is empty, so there is no type-aware linting and this diff cannot move any untouched file's result.
- **Gates, all exit 0:**
  - `check:control-bytes`
  - `check:new-line-citations` (0 new)
  - `check-changeset-presence`
  - `check:changeset-claims`: report-only. 7 pending changesets name `ListView.tsx`; I read each paragraph and none is made false.
  - `check-changeset-overwrite` and `check-changeset-no-major`
  - `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit` and `check:vi-mock-override-shape`
  - `check:test-path-roots` and `check:pending-changeset-literals`
  - `check:unreferenced-sources`
  - type-check coverage and lint coverage
- **NOT MEASURED:**
  - `check:eager-closure`: it needs a console build, so its prerequisite is not met locally. CI's Build & E2E runs it.
  - The repo-wide `pnpm test` and `pnpm lint`: CI runs them.

## Ablation (head `16865773b`, objectstack `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, WRAP mode)

The pin imports `../ListView` from source rather than a package `dist/`, so no rebuild was needed.

- **A. Both map calls replaced by a comment** (anchor 2 to 0, blob `32c639f63e65` to `b2a712d3c105`): 10 failed | 5 passed (15). The five that stayed green are the FLS, undeclared-field and control pins, which hold with or without the arm. Restore proof: the blob equals HEAD `32c639f63e65`, `git diff HEAD` is empty, and the marker count is 0.
- **B. `descriptionField` re-added to the expand twin** (anchor 1 to 0, blob to `d95c7ff453bf`): only "projects a description bound to a lookup but does not expand it" went red (1 failed | 14 passed). Restore proven the same way.
- Both runs turned red, the expected direction.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out-of-scope finding (class a), handed to the seat for filing, not fixed here:** `ObjectMap` renders the marker description as a React child, so a lookup-typed `descriptionField` crashes the popup once it is expanded (measurement above). `ObjectMap`'s map search also calls `toLowerCase()` on the description; I read that from source and did not measure it.
  - The crash is reachable today wherever every relation is expanded: `ObjectMap`'s own fetch (`buildExpandFields` with no column list, read from source), a `ListView` map with no authored columns, or one whose columns include the lookup.
  - `ObjectMap` is outside this card's surface.
- **The pending objectui#10275 changeset** lists the view bindings as "kanban, calendar, gallery, timeline and gantt fields". Once this change ships in the same release, the map is one of them too. I did not edit that changeset because it is outside this card's file surface; this card's own changeset describes the map arm.
- **Changeset:** `minor` on `@object-ui/plugin-list`, because the request shape changes.
